task.title: Prepare a Linux host for source deployment
task.shortdesc: Confirm host prerequisites and operating responsibilities before installing BPM from a repository checkout.

prereq.p: Use a Linux host where you can install Python 3.14+, Git, build tools, and curl. This runbook assumes a source checkout, not a packaged installer.

context.p: This guide describes a BPM deployment from a source checkout. Keep the checkout, runtime, data, and organization-owned platform controls under a controlled operating procedure.

step.cmd: Identify the deployment purpose and record that this is a source-based Linux deployment.

info.p: Expected result: the operations note identifies the Git checkout, runtime owner, and operating procedure.

Required tools are Git, Python 3.14+, pip, make, curl, and a shell that can run source .venv/bin/activate. The repository commands use the local virtual environment and do not require a global BPM package.

step.cmd: Create a working directory that is separate from production data and secrets.

info.p: Keep the repository checkout, .venv, and local SQLite data under a controlled path. Do not store real secrets in documentation examples or committed files.

step.cmd: Record external platform responsibilities before continuing.

info.note: Document the organization-owned procedures for services, reverse proxy and TLS, secrets, backups, restore, monitoring, and production hardening before exposing the instance to users.

result.p: The host and operating assumptions are ready for a supported BPM source checkout workflow.

postreq.p: Continue with the Linux source checkout topic before configuring runtime variables.
